paragraphs: ORIC Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to improving patients' lives by Overcoming Resistance In Cancer.

Profound advancements in oncology drug development have expanded the treatment options available to patients, yet therapeutic resistance and relapse continue to limit the efficacy and duration of clinical benefit of such treatments. Collectively, our founders and management team have a decades-long heritage of identifying and characterizing resistance mechanisms in oncology, having discovered, developed and commercialized groundbreaking medicines at companies such as Ignyta, Medivation, Aragon, Pharmacyclics, Deciphera and Genentech.

Our fully integrated research and development team is advancing a diverse pipeline of innovative clinical therapies designed to counter resistance mechanisms in cancer by leveraging our expertise within three specific areas: hormone-dependent cancers, precision oncology and key tumor dependencies.
Our clinical stage product candidates include:

• Rinzimetostat (formerly ORIC-944), an allosteric inhibitor of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) via the embryonic ectoderm development (EED) subunit, for which we licensed development and commercialization rights from Mirati Therapeutics, Inc. (Mirati) under a license agreement (Mirati License Agreement). We filed and cleared an Investigational New Drug application (IND) with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for rinzimetostat in the fourth quarter of 2021. We completed a Phase 1b trial of rinzimetostat as a single-agent, in patients with advanced prostate cancer and reported initial Phase 1b data from this trial in January 2024, demonstrating potential best-in-class drug properties, including an approximate 20-hour clinical half-life, robust target engagement and a favorable safety profile. In July 2024, we announced that in the first half of 2024 we initiated dosing of rinzimetostat in combination with apalutamide as well as in combination with darolutamide, as part of the ongoing Phase 1b trial in patients with metastatic castration resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). We also announced that we entered into clinical trial collaboration and supply agreements with Janssen Research & Development, LLC, a Johnson and Johnson company (Johnson & Johnson) and Bayer Consumer Care AG (Bayer), to evaluate rinzimetostat in combination with Erleada® (apalutamide), Johnson & Johnson's androgen receptor (AR) inhibitor, and Nubeqa® (darolutamide), Bayer's AR inhibitor. In November 2025, we announced the completion of the dose exploration portion of the Phase 1b trial and the selection of provisional recommended Phase 2 doses (RP2Ds) of rinzimetostat to be tested in combination with the approved doses of darolutamide and apalutamide in the dose optimization portion of the Phase 1b trial: 400 mg and 600 mg QD of rinzimetostat in combination with 600 mg BID of darolutamide; and 600 mg, 800 mg and 1,200 mg QD of rinzimetostat in combination with 240 mg QD of apalutamide. Also, in November 2025, we reported Phase 1b dose exploration data in 20 patients with mCRPC, who were treated with rinzimetostat in combination with 240 mg QD of apalutamide or with 600 mg BID of darolutamide. The November 2025 data set (cutoff date of September 22, 2025) demonstrated PSA responses and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) reductions across all rinzimetostat dose levels and at comparable rates in combination with apalutamide or with darolutamide. Broad and deep PSA responses were demonstrated, with 55% of patients achieving a PSA50 response rate (confirmed in 40%), and 20% of patients achieving a PSA90 response rate (all confirmed). Rapid and deep ctDNA responses were observed in patients across a breadth of AR mutations and other gene alterations, with 76% of patients achieving greater than 50% ctDNA reduction, and 59% of patients achieving ctDNA clearance. Both combination regimens demonstrated a safety profile compatible with long-term dosing, with the vast majority of treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) Grade 1 or 2 in severity and consistent with PRC2 and AR inhibition. As of the September 22, 2025 cutoff date, only one patient experienced a Grade 3 TRAE, and there were no Grade 4 or Grade 5 AEs attributed to rinzimetostat, apalutamide or darolutamide. We expect to report dose optimization data in the first quarter of 2026, and we expect to initiate our first global Phase 3 registrational trial for rinzimetostat in mCRPC in the first half of 2026.

• Enozertinib (formerly ORIC-114), a brain-penetrant, orally bioavailable, irreversible inhibitor targeting EGFR exon 20 and EGFR atypical mutations, for which we licensed development and commercialization rights from Voronoi Inc. (Voronoi) under a license and collaboration agreement (Voronoi License Agreement). In the fourth quarter of 2021, we filed a Clinical Trial Application (CTA) in South Korea for enozertinib, which was cleared in the first quarter of 2022. We also filed and cleared an IND with the FDA for enozertinib in the third quarter of 2022. Enozertinib is being evaluated in Phase 1b trials in EGFR exon 20 and P-loop and alpha C-helix compressing (PACC) mutated NSCLC, which allow enrollment of patients with CNS metastases that are either treated or untreated but asymptomatic. We

reported initial Phase 1b data with enozertinib as a monotherapy in patients with EGFR exon 20 mutations at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in October 2023, which demonstrated both systemic and intracranial activity across multiple dose levels in a heavily pre-treated patient population. In April 2024, we announced the selection of two provisional RP2Ds of enozertinib at 80 mg and 120 mg QD. In December 2025, we reported additional Phase 1b data at the 2025 ESMO Asia Congress in treatment-naïve and in previously treated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with EGFR exon 20 and EGFR atypical mutations. EGFR atypical mutations are a heterogeneous group of non-classical mutations, with PACC mutations comprising the largest subset. Enozertinib achieved highly competitive systemic response rates as well as profound antitumor activity in the CNS in EGFR exon 20 and EGFR PACC patients. Enozertinib also demonstrated a well-tolerated safety profile in EGFR exon 20 and EGFR atypical patients, with no significant off-target toxicity and manageable on-target toxicity, resulting in low rate of discontinuations. Based on these data, 80 mg QD oral enozertinib has been selected as the monotherapy dose for potential Phase 3 development. In January 2025, we announced that we entered into a clinical trial and supply agreement with Johnson & Johnson to evaluate enozertinib in combination with amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj subcutaneous injection (SC amivantamab) for the first line treatment of patients with advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 mutations, and we initiated a Phase 1b trial in the first quarter of 2025. Dosing and follow-up continues in NSCLC patients with exon 20 mutations, including as a monotherapy, in combination with SC amivantamab and in combination with chemotherapy, as well as in NSCLC patients with EGFR PACC mutations as a monotherapy. We expect to report data in the second half of 2026 in 1L NSCLC patients with EGFR exon 20 mutations as a monotherapy and in combination with SC amivantamab, as well as in 1L NSCLC patients with EGFR PACC mutations as a monotherapy.

Beyond these clinical stage product candidates, we have historically engaged in the research and development of multiple discovery stage precision medicines targeting other hallmark cancer resistance mechanisms. On August 12, 2025, we announced a strategic pipeline prioritization to focus operational and financial resources on the continued advancement of our two lead clinical programs, rinzimetostat and enozertinib. This initiative has resulted in a substantial decrease in preclinical research, primarily from the elimination of our discovery research group.

Cancer resistance continues to be one of the most daunting challenges facing patients, clinicians and researchers in oncology today. A multitude of biological factors and pathways have been linked to resistance, which enables tumors to restore cell growth and survival by circumventing a treatment's intended mechanism of action. Our resistance platform is focused on three areas: (1) innate resistance, which derives from an unaddressed oncogenic driver that promotes tumorigenesis; (2) acquired resistance, the result of an induced or enriched oncogenic driver that arises in response to treatment; and (3) bypass resistance, the activation of a compensatory signaling pathway in response to treatment.

We are building a portfolio of novel agents targeting multiple resistance mechanisms by leveraging our specialized expertise in hormone-dependent cancers, precision oncology and key tumor dependencies:

• Hormone-dependent cancers: Two of our founders, Drs. Charles Sawyers and Richard Heyman, are leading experts in nuclear hormone receptors and hormone-dependent cancers. They previously co-founded two oncology companies, Aragon (acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2013) and Seragon (acquired by Roche in 2014), that developed therapeutics targeting two nuclear hormone receptors, the AR and estrogen receptor, respectively, the former effort leading to the approved drug Erleada (apalutamide). Our product candidate rinzimetostat is an allosteric inhibitor of PRC2 with mechanism of action via binding the EED subunit that was designed to have superior drug properties compared to EZH2 inhibitors and is being developed as a potential treatment for advanced prostate cancer. Given the breadth of solid tumor indications in which hormone signaling pathways have been implicated in driving disease, or in the development of resistance, we believe our differentiated insight into this biology is a crucial component of our future success.

• Precision oncology: Our precision medicine approach of utilizing biomarkers for demonstration of target and pathway engagement and ultimately for patient selection is rooted in our management team's prior experience at Ignyta (acquired by Roche in 2018) in successfully developing Rozlytrek (entrectinib), which was approved by the FDA for the treatment of ROS1-positive metastatic NSCLC and neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase (NTRK)-positive solid tumors in 2019. Similarly, our product candidate enozertinib, a brain-penetrant, orally bioavailable irreversible inhibitor targeting EGFR exon 20 and EGFR atypical mutations, is being developed in genetically defined patient populations, including NSCLC. Our team's experience in precision oncology dates back decades, including Dr. Sawyers' pivotal role in the development of Gleevec (imatinib) and Sprycel (dasatinib). We believe our team's expertise and experience in precision oncology will allow us to develop drugs with a higher probability of clinical success within biomarker-defined patient populations, while also potentially reducing the time and cost of development.

• Key tumor dependencies: Key tumor dependencies are abnormal alterations that promote cancer cell growth and survival and also confer specific vulnerabilities that normal cells lack; these cancer-specific dependencies are compelling therapeutic targets. Our scientific team—led by our Chief Scientific Officer, head of biology and head of translational medicine—has amassed deep knowledge of key oncogenic drivers and pathways in order to identify and validate oncology targets. They most recently worked together at Genentech, where they progressed more than 20 oncology discovery programs into clinical development, with four approvals to date, including Cotellic (cobimetinib), Zelboraf (vemurafenib), Polivy (polatuzumab vedotin) and Itovebi (inavolisib). Our knowledge of innate, acquired and bypass resistance mechanisms, as well as our in-depth experience in forward and reverse translation, underpins our efforts to identify key drivers of cancer resistance that can be exploited for therapeutic gain.

We are applying our internal capabilities to these three areas of expertise to identify and develop innovative therapies targeting the critical cancer resistance mechanisms that we believe will bring the largest benefit to patients, including by making existing therapies more effective for a longer period of time.

Our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability depends significantly on our ability to achieve several objectives relating to the development and commercialization of our product candidates.

Market conditions and changing circumstances, some of which may be beyond our control, could impair our ability to access our existing cash, cash equivalents and investments and to timely pay key vendors and others.
Risks related to the development and commercialization of our product candidates

The clinical trials of our product candidates may not demonstrate safety and efficacy to the satisfaction of the FDA, EMA or other comparable foreign regulatory authorities or otherwise produce positive results.

If we experience delays or difficulties in the enrollment and/or maintenance of patients in clinical trials, our regulatory submissions or receipt of necessary marketing approvals could be delayed or prevented.
Our operations and financial results could be adversely impacted by global pandemics or other public health emergencies in the United States and the rest of the world.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and related notes and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and in our other public filings in evaluating our business. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and growth prospects. In such an event, the market price of our common stock could decline. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations and the market price of our common stock.

The following summarizes the most material risks that make an investment in our securities risky or speculative. If any of the following risks occur or persist, our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects could be materially harmed and the market price of our common stock could significantly decline:
• our limited operating history; • our past and anticipated future net losses; • uncertainty related to our ability to generate revenue and achieve profitability; and
• our need for substantial additional capital to finance our operations.
• our substantial dependence on our product candidates; • our challenges in developing and commercializing additional product candidates;
• limitations in regulatory approval processes and product candidate approvals; • our clinical trials that may fail to satisfactorily demonstrate safety and efficacy;

• payments to third parties in connection with the clinical development of our product candidates, including contract research organizations (CROs) and consultants;
• the cost of manufacturing products for use in our preclinical studies and clinical trials, including payments to contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs) and consultants;

• payments to third parties in connection with the preclinical development of our product candidates, including outsourced professional scientific development services, consulting research fees and sponsored research arrangements with third parties;

paragraphs: ORIC Pharmaceuticals 是一家臨牀階段的生技藥品公司，致力於透過克服癌症抗藥性來改善病患的生活品質。

癌症藥物開發的重大進展已拓展了病患的治療選擇，然而，治療抗藥性與復發仍持續限制這些治療的療效與臨牀效益的持續時間。 collectively，我們的創辦人與管理團隊擁有數十年的經驗，專門於識別與 characterization 抗藥性機制，在癌症領域中，已發現、開發並商業化突破性的藥物，例如在 Ignyta、Medivation、Aragon、Pharmacyclics、Deciphera 和 Genentech 等公司。
我們的完整整合研究與開發團隊正在推進一個多樣化的創新臨牀療法管道，這些療法旨在透過我們在三個特定領域的專業知識，來對抗癌症中的抗藥性機制：荷爾蒙依賴性癌症、精準醫療與關鍵腫瘤依賴性。
我們的臨牀階段產品候選藥物包括：

• Rinzimetostat（原為 ORIC-944），一種針對 polycomb repressive complex 2（PRC2）透過胚胎外胚層發育（EED）亞單位的變體抑制劑，我們已從 Mirati Therapeutics, Inc.（Mirati）取得開發與商業化權利，根據許可協議（Mirati License Agreement）。我們於 2021 年第四季向美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）提交並獲准 Investigational New Drug 申請（IND）針對 rinzimetostat。我們已完成 rinzimetostat 單一藥物在晚期前列腺癌病患的 Phase 1b 試驗，並於 2024 年 1 月報告此試驗的初步 Phase 1b 數據，顯示潛在的 best-in-class 藥物特性，包括約 20 小時的臨牀半衰期、強大的目標作用及良好的安全性。2024 年 7 月，我們宣佈在 2024 年上半年開始以 rinzimetostat 與 apalutamide 組合以及與 darolutamide 組合進行治療，作為持續進行的 Phase 1b 試驗中，針對轉移性荷爾蒙療法抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）病患的治療。我們也宣佈與 Janssen Research & Development, LLC（Johnson and Johnson 公司）及 Bayer Consumer Care AG（Bayer）簽訂臨牀試驗合作與供應協議，評估 rinzimetostat 與 Erleada®（apalutamide）以及 Nubeqa®（darolutamide）組合的療效。2025 年 11 月，我們宣佈完成 Phase 1b 試驗的劑量探索部分，並選出預備推薦的 Phase 2 劑量（RP2Ds）以進行組合治療：400 mg 和 600 mg 每日一次的 rinzimetostat 組合 600 mg 每日兩次的 darolutamide；以及 600 mg、800 mg 和 1,200 mg 每日一次的 rinzimetostat 組合 240 mg 每日一次的 apalutamide。2025 年 11 月，我們報告了 20 名 mCRPC 病患在 rinzimetostat 與 240 mg 每日一次的 apalutamide 或 600 mg 每日兩次的 darolutamide 組合治療下的 Phase 1b 劑量探索數據。2025 年 11 月的數據（截止日期為 2025 年 9 月 22 日）顯示在所有 rinzimetostat 劑量層次中，PSA 回應及循環腫瘤 DNA（ctDNA）減少率在與 apalutamide 或 darolutamide 組合治療時表現一致。廣泛且深層的 PSA 回應被觀察到，55% 的病患達到 PSA50 回應率（40% 確認），20% 的病患達到 PSA90 回應率（全部確認）。在 AR 突變及其他基因變異的病患中，觀察到快速且深層的 ctDNA 回應，76% 的病患達到大於 50% 的 ctDNA 減少，59% 的病患達到 ctDNA 清除。兩種組合療法均顯示與長期治療相容的安全性，治療相關不良事件（TRAEs）大多為 Grade 1 或 Grade 2 級別，與 PRC2 和 AR 抑制一致。截至 2025 年 9 月 22 日截止日期，僅有一名病患出現 Grade 3 TRAE，且無 Grade 4 或 Grade 5 AEs 與 rinzimetostat、apalutamide 或 darolutamide 相關。我們預期在 2026 年第一季報告劑量優化數據，並預期在 2026 年第一季開始 rinzimetostat 在 mCRPC 的第一個全球 Phase 3 登記試驗。

• Enozertinib（原為 ORIC-114），一種可穿透大腦、口服生物利用度高、不可逆的 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR 非典型突變抑制劑，我們已從 Voronoi Inc.（Voronoi）取得開發與商業化權利，根據許可與合作協議（Voronoi License Agreement）。2021 年第四季，我們在韓國提交 Clinical Trial Application（CTA）以 enozertinib 為主，並於 2022 年第一季獲准。我們也於 2022 年第三季提交並獲准 IND 以 enozertinib 為主。Enozertinib 正在評估於 EGFR exon 20 和 P-loop 和 alpha C-helix compressing（PACC）突變的非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）的 Phase 1b 試驗，允許納入有 CNS 轉移且治療或未治療但無症狀的病患。我們

在 2023 年 10 月的歐洲醫學腫瘤學會（ESMO）大會上報告了 enozertinib 單一療法在 EGFR exon 20 突變病患的初步 Phase 1b 數據，顯示在多重治療過的病患羣中，系統性和腦部活動。2024 年 4 月，我們宣佈選出 enozertinib 的兩種預備 RP2Ds，劑量為 80 mg 和 120 mg 每日一次。2025 年 12 月，我們在 2025 年 ESMO 亞洲大會上報告了額外的 Phase 1b 數據，針對未治療和先前治療的非小細胞肺癌（NSCLC）病患，其 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR 非典型突變。EGFR 非典型突變是一羣非傳統的突變，其中 PACC 突變佔最大比例。80 mg 每日一次的 enozertinib 已被選為單一療法劑量，用於潛在的 Phase 3 發展。2025 年 1 月，我們宣佈與 Johnson & Johnson 籤訂臨牀試驗與供應協議，評估 enozertinib 與 amivantamab 和 hyaluronidase-lpuj 皮下注射（SC amivantamab）組合，用於治療 EGFR exon 20 突變的晚期 NSCLC 病患，並於 2025 年第一季啟動 Phase 1b 試驗。NSCLC 病患的劑量與追蹤持續進行，包括單一療法、與 SC amivantamab 組合、與化療組合，以及 EGFR PACC 突變的 NSCLC 病患單一療法。我們預期在 2026 年第二季報告 EGFR exon 20 突變 NSCLC 病患單一療法及與 SC amivantamab 組合的數據，以及 EGFR PACC 突變 NSCLC 病患單一療法的數據。
除了這些臨牀階段產品候選藥物，我們歷來參與多個發現階段的精準醫療藥物研究與開發，針對其他癌症抗藥性機制。2025 年 8 月 12 日，我們宣佈戰略管道優先順序，專注於持續推進我們兩個主要臨牀計畫 rinzimetostat 和 enozertinib 的運作與財務資源。此舉導致預先臨牀研究大幅減少，主要來自我們發現研究小組的解散。
癌症抗藥性持續是當前腫瘤學領域患者、臨牀醫生和研究者面臨的最艱巨挑戰之一。許多生物學因素和途徑已被連結至抗藥性，這使得腫瘤能透過繞過治療的預期作用機制，恢復細胞生長與存活。我們的抗藥性平台專注於三個領域：(1) 先天抗藥性，源自未被處理的致癌驅動因子，促進腫瘤生成；(2) 獲得性抗藥性，是因治療誘導或增強的致癌驅動因子所產生；(3) 繞過抗藥性，是因治療而活化補償性訊號途徑。
我們正在建立一個針對多種抗藥性機制的創新藥物組合，透過我們在激素依賴性癌症、精準醫療和關鍵腫瘤依賴性方面的專業知識：

• 激素依賴性癌症：我們的兩位創辦人，查爾斯·賽維爾博士與理查德·海曼博士，是核激素受體與激素依賴性癌症的權威專家。他們先前共同創立了兩間腫瘤學公司，Aragon（於2013年被強生收購）與Seragon（於2014年被羅氏收購），這些公司開發了針對兩種核激素受體的治療藥物，分別為AR與雌激素受體，後者開發出已核准的藥物Erleada（阿帕魯胺）。我們的產品候選藥物rinzimetostat是一種PRC2的別構抑制劑，其作用機制為透過結合EED亞基，設計上具有較EZH2抑制劑更優越的藥物特性，並正在開發作為晚期前列腺癌的潛在治療藥物。考慮到激素訊號途徑在許多實體腫瘤中被認為是驅動疾病或產生抗藥性的因素，我們相信我們對此生物學的獨特見解是我們未來成功的關鍵零組件。

• 精準醫療：我們的精準醫療方法，透過生物標記物來展示目標與途徑的參與，並最終用於患者篩選，源於我們管理團隊在Ignyta（於2018年被羅氏收購）的先前經驗，成功開發了Rozlytrek（entrectinib），該藥物於2019年獲FDA核准用於治療ROS1陽性轉移性NSCLC及神經發育酪胺酸受體激酶（NTRK）陽性實體腫瘤。同樣地，我們的產品候選藥物enozertinib是一種能穿透腦部、口服生物可利用的不可逆抑制劑，針對EGFR exon 20及EGFR非典型突變，正在針對具有基因定義的患者族羣進行開發，包括NSCLC。我們團隊在精準醫療的經驗可追溯至數十年前，包括賽維爾博士在Gleevec（imatinib）與Sprycel（dasatinib）開發中的關鍵角色。我們相信我們團隊在精準醫療的專業知識與經驗，將使我們能開發出在生物標記定義患者族羣中具有更高臨牀成功機率的藥物，同時也可能減少開發的時間與成本。

• 關鍵腫瘤依賴性：關鍵腫瘤依賴性是促進癌細胞生長與存活的異常改變，同時也使正常細胞缺乏的特定弱點；這些癌症特有的依賴性是強大的治療目標。我們的科學團隊—由首席科學官、生物學主管與轉譯醫學主管領導—已累積對關鍵致癌驅動因子與途徑的深入知識，以識別與驗證腫瘤學目標。他們最近曾在Genentech共事，成功將超過20個腫瘤學發現計畫推進至臨牀開發，目前已獲得四項核准，包括Cotellic（cobimetinib）、Zelboraf（vemurafenib）、Polivy（polatuzumab vedotin）與Itovebi（inavolisib）。我們對先天、獲得性與繞過抗藥性機制的知識，以及我們在正向與逆向轉譯方面的深入經驗，是我們努力識別可被利用於治療獲益的癌症抗藥性關鍵驅動因子的基礎。
我們正在運用內部能力，針對這三個專業領域，以識別並開發創新療法，針對我們認為能為患者帶來最大效益的關鍵癌症抗藥性機制，包括使現有療法更有效且持續更長時間。

paragraphs: 您應配合本年度報告表10-K中所附之財務報表及相關附註，一併閱讀本節對本公司財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析。本節內容包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述，包括在「特別注意預測性陳述」節中所描述之風險。本公司實際之營運成果及部分事件之時程，可能與下文所述有重大差異。導致此等差異之因素包括，但不限於下文所列及本報告其他部分「風險因素」節中所列之因素。
ORIC Pharmaceuticals為一家臨牀階段生技藥品公司，致力於透過克服癌症之抗藥性，改善病患之生活品質。
我們完整整合之研究與開發團隊，正在推動多樣化之創新臨牀治療方案，旨在透過我們在三個特定領域之專業知識，對抗癌症之抗藥機制：荷爾蒙依賴性癌症、精準腫瘤學及關鍵腫瘤依賴性。
我們之臨牀階段產品候選藥物包括：

• Rinzimetostat (formerly ORIC-944)，一種經由 EED 子單位作用的 PRC2 零組件抑制劑，我們已自 Mirati 獲得開發與商業化權利，根據 Mirati License Agreement。我們於 2021 年第四季向 FDA 提交並獲准 IND 設立 rinzimetostat 的臨牀一期試驗。我們已完成 rinzimetostat 單一藥物用於晚期前列腺癌病患的 Phase 1b 試驗，並於 2024 年 1 月報告此試驗的初步 Phase 1b 資料，顯示其具有潛在最佳等級藥物特性，包括約 20 小時的臨牀半衰期、強大的目標作用以及良好的安全性。2024 年 7 月，我們宣佈在 2024 年第一季開始以 rinzimetostat 與 apalutamide 組合以及與 darolutamide 組合進行給藥，作為持續進行的 Phase 1b 試驗中 mCRPC 病患的治療。我們也宣佈與 Johnson & Johnson 和 Bayer 籤訂臨牀試驗合作與供應協議，評估 rinzimetostat 與 Erleada® (apalutamide)，Johnson & Johnson 的 AR 抑制劑，以及 Nubeqa® (darolutamide)，Bayer 的 AR 抑制劑組合的療效。2025 年 11 月，我們宣佈完成 Phase 1b 試驗的劑量探索部分，並選定 rinzimetostat 的 RP2Ds 用於與已核准劑量的 darolutamide 和 apalutamide 組合進行 Phase 1b 試驗的劑量最佳化部分：rinzimetostat 400 mg 和 600 mg 每日一次，與 darolutamide 600 mg 每日兩次組合；以及 rinzimetostat 600 mg、800 mg 和 1,200 mg 每日一次，與 apalutamide 240 mg 每日一次組合。2025 年 11 月，我們報告了 20 位 mCRPC 病患的 Phase 1b 劑量探索資料，這些病患接受 rinzimetostat 與 240 mg 每日一次 apalutamide 或 600 mg 每日兩次 darolutamide 組合治療。2025 年 11 月的資料集（截至 2025 年 9 月 22 日）顯示，在所有 rinzimetostat 劑量層級中，PSA 回應和 ctDNA 減少均呈現良好表現，且與 apalutamide 或 darolutamide 組合的回應率相當。廣泛且深層的 PSA 回應被觀察到，55% 的病患達到 PSA50 回應率（40% 確認），20% 的病患達到 PSA90 回應率（全部確認）。在 AR 突變和其他基因變異的廣泛範圍中，觀察到快速且深層的 ctDNA 回應，76% 的病患達到大於 50% 的 ctDNA 減少，59% 的病患達到 ctDNA 清除。兩種組合療法均顯示與長期給藥相容的安全性，絕大多數 TRAEs 為 Grade 1 或 Grade 2 級別，與 PRC2 和 AR 抑制相符合。截至 2025 年 9 月 22 日截止日期，僅有 1 位病患出現 Grade 3 TRAE，且無 Grade 4 或 Grade 5 AEs 被歸因於 rinzimetostat、apalutamide 或 darolutamide。我們預期於 2026 年第一季報告劑量最佳化資料，並預期於 2026 年第一季開始進行 rinzimetostat 在 mCRPC 的第一個全球 Phase 3 登記試驗。

• Enozertinib (formerly ORIC-114)，一種可穿透大腦、口服生物可利用、不可逆的 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR 非典型突變抑制劑，我們已自 Voronoi 獲得開發與商業化權利，根據 Voronoi License Agreement。2021 年第四季，我們在韓國提交 CTA，並於 2022 年第一季獲准。我們也於 2022 年第三季提交並獲准 IND 設立 enozertinib 的臨牀一期試驗。Enozertinib 正在進行 EGFR exon 20 和 PACC 突變 NSCLC 的 Phase 1b 試驗，允許納入有 CNS 轉移且已治療或未治療但無症狀的病患。我們在 2023 年 10 月 ESMO 大會報告 enozertinib 單一藥物用於 EGFR exon 20 突變病患的初步 Phase 1b 資料，顯示在多重治療過的病患羣中，其具有系統性和腦部活動。2024 年 4 月，我們宣佈選定 enozertinib 的兩種暫定 RP2Ds，劑量為 80 mg 和 120 mg 每日一次。2025 年 12 月，我們在 2025 年 ESMO 亞洲大會報告額外的 Phase 1b 資料，用於治療未經治療和已治療的 NSCLC 病患，這些病患具有 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR 非典型突變。EGFR 非典型突變是一羣非傳統的突變，其中 PACC 突變為最大子集。Enozertinib 在 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR PACC 病患中顯示出高度競爭性的系統反應率以及在 CNS 中深層的抗腫瘤活性。Enozertinib 也顯示出良好的安全性，

在 EGFR exon 20 和 EGFR 非典型突變病患中，無顯著的 off-target 毒性，且 on-target 毒性可管理，導致低率的中止治療。根據這些資料，80 mg 每日一次口服 enozertinib 已被選為單一藥物用於潛在 Phase 3 發展的劑量。2025 年 1 月，我們宣佈與 Johnson & Johnson 籤訂臨牀試驗與供應協議，評估 enozertinib 與 SC amivantamab 組合用於 EGFR exon 20 突變晚期 NSCLC 病患的第一線治療，並於 2025 年第一季啟動 Phase 1b 試驗。NSCLC 病患的給藥與追蹤持續進行，包括單一藥物治療、與 SC amivantamab 組合以及與化療組合，以及 EGFR PACC 突變 NSCLC 病患的單一藥物治療。我們預期於 2026 年第二季報告 EGFR exon 20 突變晚期 NSCLC 病患單一藥物治療及與 SC amivantamab 組合的資料，以及 EGFR PACC 突變晚期 NSCLC 病患單一藥物治療的資料。
除了這些臨牀階段的產品候選藥物，我們歷來參與多個發現階段的精準醫療藥物研究與開發，針對其他標誌性癌症抗藥機制。2025 年 8 月 12 日，我們宣佈策略性藥物開發路線圖優先順序，專注於持續推進我們兩大臨牀領先計畫 rinzimetostat 和 enozertinib 的運作與財務資源。此計畫導致預臨牀研究大幅減少，主要來自我們發現研究小組的取消。
研究與開發費用佔我們營運費用的很大一部分，主要為與我們產品候選藥物的發現與開發相關的外部及內部成本。
• 與我們產品候選藥物臨牀開發相關的第三方付款，包括合同研究機構（CROs）及顧問的費用；
• 用於我們臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗的產品製造成本，包括支付給合同製造機構（CMOs）及顧問的費用；
• 與我們產品候選藥物臨牀前開發相關的第三方付款，包括委外專業科學開發服務、諮詢研究費用及與第三方的贊助研究安排；
• 分配的設施、折舊及其他費用，包括IT、租金及設施維護的直接或分配費用。

與證券市場及本公司普通股持有相關之風險
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生顯著之淨虧損，且預期在可預見之未來，我們仍將產生顯著之淨虧損。
我們產生收入及實現盈利之能力，很大程度上取決於我們達成與產品候選藥物之開發及商業化相關之多項目標之能力。
市場情況及變動情形，其中一些可能超出我們之控制範圍，可能會影響我們取得現有現金、現金等價物及投資之能力，並影響我們及時支付關鍵供應商及其他方之能力。
與產品候選藥物之開發及商業化相關之風險
我們產品候選藥物之臨牀試驗可能無法顯示安全性及有效性，以符合美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）、歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）或其他相應之外國監管當局之要求，或無法產生正面結果。
若我們在臨牀試驗中遭遇 enrolment（入組）及/或 patient maintenance（患者維持）之延誤或困難，則我們之監管申請或取得必要之市場許可可能會延誤或受阻。
本公司之營運及財務結果可能因美國及全球其他地區之全球性疫情或其他公共衛生緊急事件而受到不利影響。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括我們的財務報表及其相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」的章節，並在評估我們業務時，也應參考我們其他公開的申報文件。上述任何事件或發展的發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與成長前景造成損害。在這種情況下，我們普通股的市場價格可能會下跌。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，這些也可能影響我們的業務運作與普通股的市場價格。
下列為最重大且使投資我們證券成為風險或投機性投資的風險摘要。若任何下列風險發生或持續存在，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與前景造成重大損害，並導致我們普通股的市場價格顯著下跌：
• 我們有限的營運歷史；• 我們過去及預期未來的淨虧損；• 我們能否產生收入並實現盈利的不確定性；以及
• 我們需要大量額外資金來資助營運。
• 我們對產品候選藥物的重大依賴；• 我們在開發及商業化更多產品候選藥物方面的挑戰；
• 訴訟審批程序及產品候選藥物審批的限制；• 我們的臨牀試驗可能無法令人滿意地證明其安全性與有效性；
